approval.scope: Ordinary female AMH fixed geometry and scale, canonical mini/puberty projection and mixed LH/FSH selection; no new numerical source or reference profile.

sources.reviewBasis: Repository extraction/provenance and numerical model checked; original supplementary DOCX was not freshly downloaded in this review.
sources.table: Supplementary table 1, Table D; Figure 1 age-specific GAMLSS median, not Figure 3 normalized longitudinal mean
limitations: Selected model begins at 0.02 years (approximately 7.3 days); no extrapolated numerical value at birth or prenatally.
Term infant cohort; not a preterm AMH reference.
Model median is not the biphasic relative mean trajectory used for ordinary female LH/FSH.
Infant serum and older plasma cohorts do not form one harmonized longitudinal lifespan model.

sources.population: Residual hospital samples; patients investigated for DSD or other endocrinopathy excluded. Not a healthy population birth cohort.
limitations: Small cross-sectional age groups from residual hospital samples, not a prospectively screened healthy birth cohort.
Illustration midpoint is a display convention, not an observed individual age or an age-specific model node.
Adjacent small group reversals do not establish physiological peaks or troughs.
No Tanner-specific trajectory; chronological age does not establish pubertal stage.
The pooled 1–4.9-year median does not establish an abrupt rebound immediately after the first birthday.

sources.verificationMethod: Downloaded original FDA PDF; pdftotext -layout; independent reading of Expected Reference Intervals tables and exact checks against repository values.
sources.assay: Beckman Coulter Access AMH on Access 2
sources.population: Apparently healthy nonpregnant females at five sites, regular 21–35-day menstrual cycles, both ovaries present, proven fertility.
limitations: Women were selected for regular 21–35-day cycles, both ovaries present and proven fertility; these are not all-women population medians.
Preserve plasma values consistently for older illustrative groups; do not silently substitute serum values.
Highest median belongs to the 26–30-year group; midpoint 28 is not an established exact biological peak age.
Last group is 41–45 years; no median concentrations for older women, menopause or late life are provided.
Published reference intervals exist in this FDA document, but this work does not activate or change laboratory norms.

sources.reviewBasis: Primary article metadata and abstract; no new quantitative extraction or profile.

population.timing: Premenopausal/perimenopausal visits; each woman subsequently had documented final menstrual period.

sources.supports: Declining AMH near the menopause transition, timed to individual final menstrual period.

scale.zero: baseline result point after original qualification
scale.aboveAxis: arrow with actual result, no replacement of curve or source reference
scale.boundaryTolerance: 8 machine epsilons on female AMH fixed scale only; not assay tolerance

geometry.wholeLife: Existing displaySegments retained without new anchors or refitting in whole-life coordinates.
geometry.zoom: Exact piecewise canonical Hermite-to-Bezier projection, split at source/display nodes and canonical time-axis boundaries.
geometry.mixedLHFSH: Same AMH curve projected on the selected period age axis, using its own 28.99 pmol/L scale; never IU/L or the normalized gonadotropin mean.
geometry.bridgeMeaning: Illustrative connection; source medians and their markers remain independent and may lie off the line.
geometry.olderTail: Qualitative after final FDA 41–45-year group. Display floor/timing imply no concentration, detection limit, universal menopause age or old-age plateau.
geometry.solidDashedStyles: Existing source versus illustrative segment distinction retained.

patientReference.selection: Unchanged existing reference engine, specimen/assay, age precision and censored-result qualification.
